_comment: REAL DATA, depth 2. This is the first real multi-hop chain in the corpus: Fujii's own primary RCTs support combination-efficacy claims, his 2002 review synthesises them into a general principle, and the review was then retracted BECAUSE its constituent trials were. Sources, both verified via Europe PMC: (1) the review, Fujii Y, 'Combination Antiemetic Regimens for Prevention of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting: Focus on High-Risk Patients', Clin Drug Investig 2002;22(9), doi:10.2165/00044011-200222090-00001, PMID 29492850, now marked RETRACTED ARTICLE; (2) the retraction notice, doi:10.1007/s40261-018-0634-4, PMID 29705919 (2018), which states verbatim: 'The Editor-in-Chief has retracted the original article because a number of studies [2-15] included in this review (cited as references 25-29, 31, 32, 47, 48, 50-54) have been retracted, specifically those included in table III, table IV, section 3 and section 4.2. This has rendered the content of the review scientifically unreliable.' That sentence is unusually good ground truth: it scopes the damage to named tables and sections rather than just voiding the paper.

symbols.label: 5-HT3 receptor antagonist combined with a traditional antiemetic at a different receptor
antiemetic combination acting at different emetogenic receptors
combination of traditional antiemetics (antihistamine, butyrophenone, benzamide)

surface_forms: The efficacy of a combination of a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist and dexamethasone is superior to that of 5-HT3 receptor antagonists alone for the prevention of PONV.
propositions.notes: LEVEL 1, primary-trial claim. Rests on Fujii's own RCTs, which are among the retracted references.

surface_forms: The combination of a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist with a traditional antiemetic acting at a different emetogenic receptor is more effective in reducing the incidence of PONV than each antiemetic alone acting at one receptor site.
A combination of antiemetics with different sites of activity is more effective than one drug alone for prophylaxis against postoperative nausea and vomiting.
propositions.notes: LEVEL 2, the review's general synthesised principle, derived from the two level-1 claims via D-REVIEW-SYNTHESIS. THIS IS THE SAME CLAIM as P-SYNERGISM in corpus/fujii-ponv.json, reached from a different document. Nothing in the pipeline currently notices that, which is the canonicalization problem appearing for real the moment a second corpus was added. Recorded as a finding, not silently deduplicated. Note also it carries INDEPENDENT refuting evidence from Carlisle 2012, so on retraction it should go to REFUTED rather than merely UNRESOLVED.

surface_forms: The risk of undesirable adverse effects does not increase with the combination of a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist and another antiemetic.
propositions.notes: LEVEL 2 safety claim, also derived from the retracted trial series. polarity=negate: the claim is that risk does NOT increase. Safety claims resting on fabricated data are the most consequential kind of collapse, which is why this one is included.

surface_forms: The clinical use of combined traditional antiemetics, including antihistamines, butyrophenones and benzamides, for the prevention of PONV is limited because of the possibility of additive central nervous system toxicity, such as delayed emergence, drowsiness and extrapyramidal reactions.
propositions.notes: THE CONTROL CLAIM. General pharmacology about class side effects, not an efficacy finding from Fujii's trials. GOLD LABEL IS PENDING, deliberately: the retraction notice scopes the damage to 'table III, table IV, section 3 and section 4.2', and confirming this claim sits outside those sections needs the full text, which is paywalled. Encoded with non-Fujii evidence so the reasoner treats it as surviving, but that placement is an assumption and is flagged as unverified rather than scored as gold.

rules.name: review synthesis from constituent trials
rules.notes: A narrative review generalising from its included trials is NOT logical entailment, so relation=GENERALIZES and validity=UNVERIFIED. This is exactly the distinction v0.3's Rule/Derivation split exists to keep: an informal synthesis must not be able to masquerade as a proof.

derivations.notes: The review's own inferential step, from its tables III and IV to its general principle. Its validity as a step is unchanged by the retraction; what changes is whether its premises still carry warrant.
Adverse-effect reporting in the same retracted trials.
